title: Quantitative Evaluation of Paracrine Senescence on Cellular Reprogramming
author: Chantrel, Chen, et al.

steps.title: Derive MEFs from embryos
steps.instruction: Isolate mouse embryonic fibroblasts (MEFs) from 13.5‑day‑post‑coitum WT and i4F embryos following standard protocol.

steps.title: Induce senescence in WT MEFs
steps.instruction: Treat WT MEFs with the chosen senescence‑inducing stress (e.g., irradiation, oncogene expression) as described elsewhere to generate senescent cells.

steps.title: Prepare senescent MEF culture medium
steps.instruction: Mix DMEM (100 % stock) with fetal bovine serum (FBS) to a final 10 % (v/v) and add Penicillin/Streptomycin to a final 0.45 % (45 U/mL). For 500 mL total, combine 450 mL DMEM, 50 mL FBS, and 2.5 mL Pen/Strep. Store at 4 °C up to 3 months.

steps.title: Prepare conditioned medium collection
steps.instruction: Combine DMEM (100 % stock) with KnockOut™ Serum Replacement (KSR) to a final 5 % (v/v) and Pen/Strep to 0.45 % (45 U/mL). For 500 mL, mix 450 mL DMEM, 25 mL KSR, and 2.5 mL Pen/Strep. Aliquot and store at –20 °C up to 1 month.

steps.title: Prepare iPSC reprogramming medium
steps.instruction: To 500 mL DMEM add KSR to 14.85 % (v/v), Pen/Strep to 0.49 % (49 U/mL), non‑essential amino acids (NEAA) 1× (6 mL, 0.99 % of total), GlutaMAX 1× (6 mL, 0.99 % of total), β‑mercaptoethanol 98.97 µM (1.2 mL, 0.20 %), and Leukemia Inhibitory Factor (LIF) 989.67 U/mL (60 µL). Adjust final volume to 606.26 mL with DMEM. Store at 4 °C up to 2 months.

steps.title: Prepare conditioned iPSC medium (10 mL)
steps.instruction: Take 8.279 mL senescent conditioned medium, add KSR to reach 15 % (1.5 mL), NEAA 1× (100 µL), GlutaMAX 1× (100 µL), β‑mercaptoethanol 2 µM (20 µL, 0.20 %), and LIF 1 µL (1000 U/mL). Mix to a final volume of 10 mL immediately before use.

steps.title: Prepare doxycycline stock
steps.instruction: Dissolve doxycycline hyclate to 1 mg/mL in sterile H₂O, aliquot, and store at –20 °C for up to 2 years.

steps.title: Prepare SA‑β‑Gal fixation buffer
steps.instruction: Make 320 mL fixation solution by mixing 20 mL 2 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) with 1.28 mL 0.2 % glutaraldehyde in PBS, then bring to 320 mL with PBS. Store at 4 °C up to 6 months.

steps.title: Prepare SA‑β‑Gal staining buffer
steps.instruction: Freshly prepare 10 mL staining solution containing 4 mM K₃Fe(CN)₆ (400 µL of 100 mM stock), 4 mM K₄Fe(CN)₆ (400 µL of 100 mM stock), 2 mM MgCl₂ (20 µL of 1 M stock, filtered 0.20 µm), 0.4 mg/mL X‑Gal (80 µL of 50 mg/mL stock), 0.1 % NP‑40 (10 µL of 100 % stock), in PBS adjusted to pH 5.5 (9.09 mL PBS). Use the same batch for all sections.

steps.title: Prepare IHC blocking solution
steps.instruction: Combine 300 µL 10 % Triton X‑100 (to give 0.3 % final), 1 mL normal goat serum (10 % final), and 200 µL BSA (0.2 % final) in PBS and bring to a final volume of 10 mL. Prepare fresh before use.

steps.title: SA‑β‑Gal staining of muscle cryosections
steps.instruction: Perform the following substeps on 10 µm muscle sections:

substeps.instruction: Allow tissue‑freezing medium to evaporate for 30 min at room temperature (20‑25 °C).
Circle each section with a hydrophobic DAKO pen.
Fix in SA‑β‑Gal fixation buffer for 15 min at room temperature (do not exceed 15 min; do not replace with 4 % PFA).
Quickly wash three times with PBS (<1 min per wash).
Incubate in SA‑β‑Gal staining buffer at 37 °C protected from light for 48 h; cover the container with aluminum foil.
Refresh the staining solution after 24 h.
Monitor under an inverted microscope; when blue color becomes visible, wash three times with PBS.
Note: pH must be 5.5; incubation time may vary with tissue thickness. Keep all sections stained with the same buffer batch.

steps.title: Immunohistochemistry for Nanog (or F4/80)
steps.instruction: After SA‑β‑Gal staining, execute the following substeps:

substeps.instruction: Wash three times with PBS, then post‑fix in 4 % PFA in PBS for 15 min at room temperature (max 15 min).
Wash three times with PBS.
Place slides in a humid dark chamber.
Add 200 µL blocking buffer to each circled area; incubate ≥30 min at room temperature.
Prepare primary Nanog antibody at 1:200 in blocking buffer.
Remove blocking buffer and add 200 µL primary antibody to each area (add blocking buffer only to control sections).
Incubate overnight at 4 °C in the humid dark chamber.
Bring chamber to room temperature for 20–30 min, then wash three times with PBST (PBS + 0.3 % Triton X‑100).
Incubate with 3 % H₂O₂ in PBS for 20 min at room temperature.
Add ready‑to‑use secondary antibody (Dako K4003) for 90 min at room temperature in the humid dark chamber.
Prepare DAB substrate by adding 20 µL DAB concentrate to 1 mL buffer (protect from light).
Wash three times with PBST, 5 min each.
Develop with DAB for 1 min at room temperature, then wash three times with Milli‑Q water.
Counterstain with Fast‑red for 10 min at room temperature.
Wash in tap water for 10 min.
Dehydrate: 95 % ethanol 10 min, then 100 % ethanol twice, 5 min each.
Mount with Eukitt and let cure overnight in a fume hood.
Scan slides with an Olympus VS120 scanning microscope.
Adjust primary antibody dilutions and DAB development time as needed for each antibody.
Select one representative cryosection image.
Crop a region adjacent to the tissue edge and save three copies as file1.jpg, file2.jpg, and t1.jpg in a folder named cfg_fig6.
Using an image editor (e.g., Fiji, Paint, Paint X), draw black scribbles on the outside of the muscle section in file1.jpg and save as file1_bk.jpg.
Draw black scribbles inside the muscle section in file2.jpg and save as file2_inside.jpg.
Mark SA‑β‑Gal‑positive cells with white dots on t1.jpg and save as t1_pt.jpg.
Use the same reference image for all analyses; reset references if sample coloration changes.

steps.title: Run Showblue quantification
steps.instruction: Follow Methods video S1 (or the YouTube link https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BHaThFfpkRY) to launch Showblue, load the cfg_fig6 folder, set preferences, run a test image, adjust parameters if false positives/negatives appear, then batch‑process all images. Perform quantification blinded and analyze statistics with GraphPad Prism v9.
